newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DON JUMPS ON EXPECTED RIGHTS OFFER -DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: DON JUMPS ON EXPECTED RIGHTS OFFER -DEALERS.

text.p: Shares in South African apartment and restaurant firm Don Group Ltd rocketted on Thursday as players anticipated it would hold a rights issue, the proceeds of which could boost the company, dealers said.
Don's shares touched a high of 180 cents from a 122 cents overnight, but slipped off their highs to close at 142 cents -- a gain of 20 cents on the day.
"(The company) is hoping to have a rights issue," one dealer said.
"They are pushing the share price ahead so that they can get a good price for the offer. They need capital and they are a bit cash-strapped," one dealer said.
Don's share price has come back heavily from around 500 cents in September last year, touching a low of 88 cents last month as the hotel sector suffers amid fierce competition.
A spokesman for the firm declined to comment on whether it was planning a rights issue but added that there would be an official company announcement within a few days.
Dealers said there could be some restructuring on the cards or that Don may sell some of its food businesses as announced in May.
Don said at the time it was negotiating with several interested organisations to take over its restaurant brands as it was believed they would do better in a new food-related grouping.
Its restaurant brands include Squire's, Giuseppe's, RJ's and Al's.
The share is also currently trading under a cautionery that it was in talks with property developer Sable Holdings Ltd . No further details have been released on the talks.
